title: Elevator domain model
idea: The elevator domain model separates the fixed building (Floor), the moving parts (Elevator with state and stops) and short-lived calls (Request), coordinated by one ElevatorController.

analogy.text: A bus line. The stops never move, each bus knows where it is and where it heads, and every stop bell lasts until it is served.
analogy.breaks: A bus follows a fixed route; an elevator reverses on demand.

points: A Floor is a value: its number and which hall buttons it has.
A hall Request has UP or DOWN; a car Request has IDLE.
An Elevator owns its floor, Direction, ElevatorState and a sorted set of stops.
ElevatorController holds the cars and asks a SchedulingStrategy which car answers.

edges.label: has 1
edges.caption: The controller serves one building. The building owns the floors.

edges.label: has 1..*
edges.caption: Each Floor is an immutable record. The top floor has no UP button.

edges.label: has 1..*
edges.caption: The controller holds every car. Cars never move between controllers.

edges.label: has 1
edges.caption: ElevatorState says what the car is doing now: idle, moving, doors open, or out.

edges.label: has 1
edges.caption: Direction is separate from state. An idle car can still face UP.

edges.label: at 1
edges.caption: A Request points at one Floor. Hall calls carry a Direction; car calls do not.

edges.label: uses 1
edges.caption: Choosing a car is a swappable policy. Page 3 implements it.

code.title: The model in Java 17
code.caption: Records and enums for values, a class for Elevator because it changes. Invariants live in constructors.

walk.text: Build a ten-floor building, two cars, and the controller that owns them.
One hall call and one car call become stops on E1. E2 has none.
Two bad inputs are refused: UP on the top floor, and floor 12.
The compact constructor checks each request against the buttons its floor has.
Two factories build the two kinds; a car call is always IDLE.
Elevator keeps stops in a TreeSet, so the next stop either way is cheap.
The controller holds an immutable car list. The strategy is filled in next page.

pitfalls: Do not store waiting people on Floor; store each call as a Request.
Keep stops in a sorted set; an unsorted list makes the next stop slow.
Reject impossible requests in constructors, such as UP on the top floor.

quiz.q: What does the third line of DomainModel print?
quiz.why: Adding a stop only records it; nothing ticks, so E1 stays at floor 0. The TreeSet keeps stops sorted, so 3 comes before 7.

takeaway: Floors are fixed, Elevators hold state, Requests are short-lived.

starters: Why is Direction separate from ElevatorState?
Should a car call and a hall call be two classes instead of one Request?
Where would passenger weight and capacity checks go?
